messages:
devon: quick follow-up from the all-hands — a few clarifying q's about the org shift and hiring priorities
maya: thanks for pulling these up, devon. high level: we want to preserve the runtime/infra specialization but unify reporting for faster decisions. details below. cc @jordan @lee
devon: 1) will Platform Eng stay split into Runtime + Serving pods or be collapsed under a single director?
maya: runtime + serving remain separate teams day-to-day. they will report into a new Head of Platform (single exec) to align strategy and tradeoffs across Dedicated/Private/Hosted. this is to avoid duplicate work while keeping deep technical ownership with each pod.
jordan: to add — leads keep hiring autonomy for their backlog priorities, but strategic trades will go through the platform head for consistency.
devon: 2) if folks transfer between teams, how are backfills prioritized? some managers already have open reqs.
lee: People Ops plan: we will prioritize backfills for revenue-impacting and customer-SLA roles first. then cross-team critical skills (runtime kernels, model-onboarding infra). greenfield or noncritical backfills are deprioritized until Q3 budget recheck. we'll publish a priority matrix today.
sam: small note: if a manager needs an immediate backfill due to production risk, file a short case to #hq-hiring with the tag "urgent-backfill" and we'll fast-track review.
devon: 3) internal mobility window — when does that open and how long?
maya: internal mobility window opens next Monday for five working days. managers should expect transfer conversations to start the week after. people opting to interview internally will be given a clear SLA for decisions (2 weeks) to reduce uncertainty.
irene: will current external offers in the pipeline be affected? we've seen candidates in final loops.
jordan: offers already extended or in final stage will be honored. recruiting should continue closing existing candidates. budgets for those roles are committed until the mobility window completes.
devon: 4) what about career ladder / role regrades for ICs impacted by new reporting lines?
maya: we will run calibration & regrade sessions next week (invite to managers & IC reps this afternoon). anyone who thinks their role is materially different should raise it with their manager; we will have an expedited review path for regrade requests tied to the reorg.
devon: any change to on-call or rotation expectations? some teams are worried about load.
jordan: no immediate increase to on-call load. we will consolidate rotation leads to remove duplication, aim to keep total pages stable. any team facing >15% delta in pager load will get temporary hire/handoff support.
lee: People Ops will publish a FAQ + mobility checklist (links + templates) by EOD. people-bot: https://intranet.redwood.com/people/mobility-faq :link:
devon: thanks — last thing: timeline for the updated org chart and who to ask about role mapping?
maya: updated org map tomorrow morning in the all-hands folder, and a "who owns what" CSV for mapping. questions about individual mappings should start with your manager; escalations go to people-ops@redwood.
devon: appreciate the quick answers. will share these notes in the follow-up doc and tag folks for any clarifications :thumbsup:
maya: thanks everyone. we'll keep the updates frequent and short so teams can plan.
